subject: Post-demo: platform economics, comparative unit costs & proposed test plan
messages:
From: Jane Moss <jane.moss@acmeretail.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Demo follow-up + cost comparison ask

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. The team liked the routing/fallback flow and the caching examples — that part of the product maps directly to a few of our latency-sensitive recommender paths. Before we carve out testing windows, procurement and our platform team need a clear, side-by-side unit economics view and a short proposed test plan. Two asks to unblock internally: 

1) Per-1M token cost comparison (hosted inference) vs the two options we're evaluating (vendor-managed endpoints on AWS and managed endpoints on GCP). We need a simple table we can share with finance: assumptions like average prompt+completion length, batching assumptions, and whether KV/prefix cache is included in the price.

2) A proposed A/B test that demonstrates the latency/cost tradeoffs — our targets: p95 < 400ms for 95th percentile recommendations, and an operating budget that doesn't exceed $X/month (we'll share number with finance once we have a per-1M baseline).

I've attached the deck from our side showing the flows we want to test (redwood-demo-deck.pdf). Can you send a one-page economics comparison + a short test plan we can use to get internal approvals?

Tom (cc'd) will be coordinating procurement.

Appreciate it —
Jane Moss
Head of AI, Acme Retail
---

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-02T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + cost comparison ask

Jane — thanks for the clear asks and the deck. Quick recap and a recommendation for the test (high level) so your team has something to circulate to finance/procurement: 

Summary (short): Redwood offers predictable unit economics when you account for automatic batching + prefix/KV caching. Below is a preliminary per-1M token view (hosted inference, standard model family we showed):

- Redwood Hosted (default config): ~$16.50 per 1M tokens
  - Assumptions: avg prompt+response = 1,200 tokens; average continuous batching (effective batch size 6–8) and prefix cache hit = 40% after warmup
- AWS-managed endpoints (raw GPU endpoints): ~$34–40 per 1M tokens
  - Assumptions: no cross-request prefix cache by default, batching depends on infra config (we assumed batch size 4–6), and additional infra egress/overhead not included
- GCP-managed endpoints (comparable offering): ~$30–36 per 1M tokens

Notes: these are ballpark list economics to compare unit costs. The main drivers are batching efficiency and cache hit (%). Small changes to average batch size or cache hit produce ~10–30% swing in unit cost.

Proposed 7-day POC (recommended / minimal scope):
- Goal: prove p95 latency and unit cost delta under representative production load
- Traffic pattern: 200k tokens/day (peak concurrent users aligned with your traffic spike window)
- Test setup: A/B between Redwood hosted and AWS-managed endpoint (routing 50/50). Same model family and prompt sets.
- Success metrics: p95 latency < 400ms for >=95% of requests on Redwood side; measured per-1M token cost delta >= 20% savings vs AWS at target batch/cache behavior.
- Data collection: token counts, p50/p95 latencies, avg batch size, observed cache hit rate (prefix hits), error rates, and cost estimate sample by day

Immediate next steps I propose from our side:
- Redwood: provide an instrumentation script + minimal load harness to run in your environment (we'll share a small Dockerized harness and a results sheet).
- Procurement: we can pre-fill an MAA/draft SOW (Rishi will share an initial file).
- Timing: if you approve, we can stand up the Redwood side of the A/B by next Tuesday (2027-04-06).

I'll attach a compact one-pager with the cost assumptions and a checklist for the run. If you want me to flip the table into a format your finance team prefers (line items), say the word and I'll reformat.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0186

Marcus / Rishi —

This is helpful and aligns with what finance wanted to see. A few clarifications and a formal test ask so we can get approvals tomorrow: 

1) Test scope (P0): 7-day A/B run comparing Redwood hosted vs AWS-managed endpoint
   - Traffic envelope: ~200k tokens/day (controlled harness), ramp in 3 steps across 24 hours
   - Objective: measure p50/p95 latency, average batch size, observed cache hit rate, and per-1M token cost estimate

2) Success criteria (what finance/platform care about):
   - Redwood side: p95 latency < 400ms for >=95% of calls
   - Cost: confirmed per-1M delta >= 20% savings vs AWS with observed batching/cache behavior (if delta smaller we escalate to architecture discussion)

3) Measurement and instrumentation: we'll run your harness in our test VPC and provide logs (token counts + latency traces). We need an exported CSV at the end of each day with the following columns: date, tokens_generated, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, avg_batch_size, cache_hit_rate_pct, estimated_cost_usd

4) Timing: procurement will try to sign the MAA appendix for a POC rate once we see final line items. Rishi — please send the DocuSign path / rough timeline for procurement review.

If you can confirm the instrumentation format and share the harness by end of day (2027-04-05), we'll queue platform resources and schedule the A/B run for 2027-04-08.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Jane Moss
Head of AI, Acme Retail
